data.name: Restoration
data.detailed_description:
A young man with the title of "Dream-Catcher" is tasked to restore souls on the brink of despair by purifying their hearts and preventing them from becoming nightmares, hellish beings who prey upon the weak.
On the outside, the land seems painted with hope. If you take a closer look, it will reveal that it is void of said hope. Two high school students answer a request that will change their lives forever. Join Oliver and Penello as they travel upon the region of Astrelia and use the power of Restoration to bring back the souls of the desolate beings void of hope. Touch fleeting hearts and make them glow once more on a pilgrimage of fantastic proportions. Will the siblings have what it takes to bring peace back to Astrelia or will they succumb to the darkness? Find out in Restoration.

Features:
~Colorful World.
~*Semi-Original Soundtrack.
~Simple and Sweet.
~Touching Story.
~Several Challenging Tasks.
~Difficulty Slider.

data.short_description: Two siblings; Oliver and Penello, answer their dying Grandma's wish and make their way to Phren Village. A seemingly peaceful village filled with tranquility. But on the inside, It is a village void of hope and on the brink of succumbing to despair and darkness.

reviews.review:
Restoration is a small JRPG from Team Syukino that caught my attention because of its story about people losing hope and slowly being turned into nightmares. I play as Oliver and Penello, two siblings who travel through the region of Astrelia after answering their grandmother's final request. The main idea is that I use the power of Restoration to purify the hearts of people who are close to giving in to despair. It is a simple setup, but I like the darker idea underneath the colourful presentation.

The story is probably the strongest reason for me to keep going. The game is clearly interested in themes like hope, despair and helping people who have reached a really bad point in their lives. I like that the Restoration idea is connected directly to the story instead of just being a random gameplay mechanic. The journey through Astrelia gives me different situations to deal with, and the relationship between Oliver and Penello gives the adventure a bit more personality. It is not a massive epic RPG, but there is enough of an idea here to make the world worth exploring.

The actual RPG gameplay is fairly simple, which is both good and bad for me. I can explore, deal with enemies and work through different tasks while progressing through the story. There are also several challenging tasks and a difficulty slider, so I can adjust the experience depending on how much of a challenge I want. I appreciate having that option because the game is clearly designed to be approachable rather than overwhelming me with dozens of complicated systems.

The presentation has a nice little charm to it as well. The game uses colourful anime style visuals and a 2D presentation, which fits the kind of smaller JRPG it is trying to be. I do not think the graphics are anything amazing, but they give the characters and locations enough personality to keep things pleasant. The soundtrack is also described as a semi original soundtrack, and I think that fits the smaller scale of the project. It feels like a game made around its story and atmosphere rather than trying to impress me with huge production values.

My biggest problem is that the game feels limited compared with a larger JRPG. The combat and RPG systems are fairly straightforward, so there is not a huge amount of room for me to experiment with character builds or complicated strategies. The world also feels more like a series of story locations than a massive place that I can freely explore. That is not necessarily a problem for a smaller game, but it does mean I am mostly playing for the story and atmosphere rather than because the gameplay itself is incredibly deep.

I also think the game could have done more with its central idea. The concept of restoring people who are close to becoming nightmares is genuinely interesting, and I would have liked to see even more situations built around that mechanic. There is a good emotional idea underneath the game, but some of the simpler RPG elements stop it from reaching the same level as the stronger story focused games I have played. The free availability also makes the limitations easier for me to accept because I am not being asked to pay a premium for what is ultimately a fairly modest RPG. Restoration was released in 2017 and is now listed as free on Steam.

Overall, Restoration is a pleasant little JRPG with a surprisingly thoughtful idea at its centre. I like the story about hope and despair, the relationship between the two siblings, the colourful presentation and the simple RPG structure. It is definitely limited in terms of depth and scale, and I think the Restoration concept could have been used in much more interesting ways, but there is enough personality here to make the journey worthwhile. I would not put it alongside my favourite RPGs, but I think it is a decent small adventure that works best when I focus on its story rather than expecting a huge amount of mechanical depth.

Rating: 7/10
